description:
Goal
Ship a controlled beta rollout of Hosted/Dedicated data residency enforcement (region pinning + runtime enforcement) with:
- Feature flags + safe defaults
- Canary cohorts and staged enablement
- Monitoring gates (health + customer-impact)
- Clear rollback criteria and playbooks

Scope
- Hosted API gateway enforcement + policy evaluation + smart routing constraints + downstream write enforcement are all behind coordinated flags.
- Includes enable/disable procedures for support/SRE, including customer-scoped toggles.
- Includes canary selection rules and dashboards/alerts to monitor for regressions.

Out of scope
- Customer comms templates and packaging language (tracked in PM-482 initiative + Product/Docs work)
- Any automated region migration of historic artifacts

Rollout Principles
- Fail-closed for pinned orgs/projects (deny if request would violate residency), but gating ensures we do not accidentally block non-pinned traffic.
- Deterministic behavior when pinned: no cross-region fallback unless an explicit exception/override is enabled and auditable.
- Rollout should first exercise observability-only mode to validate signals, then enforce on an internal cohort, then external pilots.

Implementation Plan
1) Feature flags (flag names + semantics)
A. residency.enforcement_enabled (global kill-switch)
- When OFF: residency check middleware does not deny; tags requests with would_deny=true/false for shadow evaluation (where supported).
- When ON: middleware enforces deny for violations.

B. residency.policy_evaluator_required (controls fallback behavior)
- When ON: gateway requires a valid policy decision; if policy evaluator is unreachable/timeout -> fail closed for pinned orgs, fail open for non-pinned.
- When OFF: gateway can proceed using cached/stale policy or default allow (intended only for early staging).

C. residency.disable_cross_region_fallback_when_pinned (routing constraint)
- When ON: router will not select non-approved regions for pinned/allowed_regions policies.
- When OFF: existing behavior, but emits audit event when a pinned org would have crossed region (shadow mode where possible).

D. residency.allow_cross_region_fallback_override (exception pathway)
- When ON + per-org override present: router may cross-region for capacity exhaustion with explicit reason codes + audit event residency.exception_used.
- Guardrails: must require Security/GRC approval and must be time-bound (expiry enforced by config validation).

E. residency.downstream_writes_enforced (storage/logging side effects)
- When ON: downstream writers (analytics/log persistence/trace export) must select in-region sinks for pinned orgs; otherwise fail the write path and emit audit event (do not re-route to cross-region sink).
- Note: must not block request completion for non-critical analytics writes unless contract requires; align with Security PM on “in-scope data” definition.

2) Canary cohort definitions
Cohort 0: Internal staging + dogfood
- Redwood employees/orgs (internal tenants) pinned to eu-west and us-east.
- Purpose: validate routing constraints, error contract, audit payloads.

Cohort 1: Internal production canary (1% of eligible traffic)
- Eligibility: org has explicit pinned_region or allowed_regions configured.
- Selection: hash(org_id) % 100 < 1, excluding any org with known multi-region clients until SDK region hint work lands.

Cohort 2: External beta pilots (hand-selected)
- List maintained by CS/Sales pilot tracker; enablement requires:
  - Signed beta acknowledgement
  - Confirmed correct base URL/SDK region setting
  - Confirmed SIEM export needs + audit event sample review

Cohort 3: Expanded beta (10% of eligible pinned orgs)
- After stability for 7 days at Cohort 2.

Cohort 4: GA readiness gate (50% then 100% of eligible pinned orgs)
- Must meet SLO + violation-noise criteria, and Support runbook readiness.

3) Enablement steps (runbook-style)
- Preflight:
  - Confirm dashboards loaded and alerts configured (Grafana panels + alert rules in observability-pack).
  - Confirm audit log exporter includes residency events.
  - Confirm support playbook has the correct error codes + remediation language.

- Step 1 (shadow mode):
  - residency.enforcement_enabled = OFF
  - Emit metrics/tags for would-deny decisions at gateway + router.
  - Validate baseline would-deny rate is near expected (mostly misconfigured region hints / wrong endpoint).

- Step 2 (internal enforce):
  - Enable enforcement for Cohort 0 only (org-scoped toggle) for 48 hours.

- Step 3 (production canary enforce):
  - residency.enforcement_enabled = ON for Cohort 1
  - residency.disable_cross_region_fallback_when_pinned = ON for Cohort 1

- Step 4 (pilot ramp):
  - Per-org enablement for Cohort 2 with Support on standby.

4) Monitoring gates (what we watch + thresholds)
Gate A: Residency violation rate (deny) for enforced cohort
- Metric: residency_gateway_decisions_total{decision="deny"} / residency_gateway_decisions_total
- Threshold: < 0.5% sustained for 30m after each ramp step (higher during first hour acceptable if tied to a single org rollout; must be investigated).
- Drilldown: by org_id (top offenders), by requested_region vs pinned_region.

Gate B: False positives / regressions
- Metric: residency_error_code_total{code="RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH"}
- Threshold: no increase in non-pinned orgs (should remain ~0). If non-pinned sees denials => immediate rollback.

Gate C: Control plane / policy evaluator health
- Metrics: policy_evaluator_request_latency_p95, policy_evaluator_errors_total
- Threshold: p95 < 50ms, error rate < 0.1%. If policy evaluator error spikes cause fail-closed denials for pinned orgs => rollback to cached mode or disable requirement.

Gate D: Routing/capacity impact
- Metrics: router_selection_failures_total, router_capacity_exhaustion_total, fallback_attempts_total
- Threshold: no sustained increase in selection failures for pinned orgs; if capacity exhaustion rises and causes customer-visible 429/5xx, consider enabling exception workflow (not cross-region by default).

Gate E: Overall API SLO impact
- Metrics: gateway_5xx_rate, p95 latency, request_timeouts
- Threshold: no statistically significant regression vs baseline for the cohort.

5) Rollback criteria (explicit)
Immediate rollback (P0) if any of:
- Denies observed for orgs with no residency policy configured.
- Spike in 5xx attributable to residency middleware/policy calls.
- Policy evaluator outage/latency causes widespread denials.

Rollback actions (order):
- Flip residency.enforcement_enabled = OFF globally (kill-switch).
- Keep shadow evaluation on if safe (for diagnosis) but stop denials.
- If needed: also disable residency.disable_cross_region_fallback_when_pinned to restore routing behavior.
- Communicate in #eng-releases + #support + incident channel if customer-impacting.

6) Audit/compliance evidence readiness
- Must emit audit events for:
  - residency.policy_evaluated (allow/deny)
  - residency.violation (deny)
  - residency.exception_used (only if explicit override enabled)
- Evidence checklist for pilots:
  - Sample payload to customer
  - SIEM export confirmation
  - Retention confirmation (per enterprise plan)

Owners / DRI
- Rollout orchestration + flag plumbing: Jada Williams (DRI)
- Release train + change mgmt: Connor O'Brien
- SRE monitoring + alerts: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Product/Security sign-off (policy semantics, exception workflow): Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov

Acceptance Criteria
- Flags exist with documented semantics and tested toggles (global + org-scoped).
- Canary cohorts defined and implementable via config/feature-flag targeting.
- Dashboards and alerts are in place; on-call knows what to do.
- Rollback documented with a 5-minute “stop the bleeding” procedure.
- Completed dry run in staging demonstrating: enable -> observe -> rollback, with screenshots/notes linked.

Notes / Risks
- High risk of noisy violation spikes due to customers using the wrong regional base URL or SDK default region. Mitigation: SDK region hint guidance + improved error payload remediation link.
- Need alignment on fail-open vs fail-closed when policy evaluator is unavailable; current stance: pinned fail-closed, non-pinned fail-open. This must be explicitly communicated to Support and included in incident response.
comments: 2025-02-05 (Connor O'Brien): Created rollout ticket to centralize flags + gating so we don’t do ad-hoc enablement per team. Linking to PM-482 for milestone alignment. Assigning Jada for rollout backend wiring.

2025-02-10 (Jada Williams): Drafted flag taxonomy based on current PR 18563 scaffolding. Added proposal for policy_evaluator_required to control fail-closed behavior. Requesting sign-off from Naomi/Marcus on evaluator outage semantics.

2025-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: please ensure metrics include org_tier + region labels but keep cardinality bounded (no raw org_id in Prometheus). For org-level drilldown, use logs/audit events + BigQuery panels. Add alert suppression guidance for first 60 minutes after ramp.

2025-02-14 (Marcus Lin): Security: OK with pinned fail-closed when evaluator unavailable, but only if we have explicit, customer-visible error code (not generic 500). Also require audit event for deny reason = POLICY_EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE to support evidence during incidents.

2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Added proposed thresholds to SRE sheet; suggest gate on overall 5xx delta for cohort rather than absolute to avoid noise. Also need a hard rollback condition if non-pinned orgs see any residency denies.

2025-02-20 (Naomi Feldman): Product: agree with no cross-region fallback by default for pinned. Exception path must be time-bound + approval required; please ensure flag + config supports expiry date validation so we can show auditors it’s not open-ended.
2025-02-26 (Jada Williams): Implemented cohort targeting in rollout tooling (internal canary + hashed sampling) behind admin-only endpoint. Pending review from Connor + SRE on operational steps.

2025-03-03 (Connor O'Brien): Ran staging dry-run: enabled shadow mode -> observed would-deny counts from misconfigured EU org calling US base URL -> toggled enforce -> saw RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH with docs link -> rollback successful. Captured notes in #eng-releases thread_1738692201. Marking ready for In Review.

2025-03-07 (Dev Patel): Support readiness request: please add a one-liner to rollback procedure for Support to confirm if issue is residency-related (look for x-redwood-error-code + audit event residency.violation). Also confirm who can flip org-scoped overrides after hours.

2025-03-10 (Jada Williams): Updated rollback section with Support quick-check + permissions note: on-call SRE can flip global kill-switch; Support can request org-level toggle via #eng-oncall with template. Moving to In Review for final approvals.
